sources.note: Local-government source checked for Arrernte traditional ownership in the Mparntwe context and living community culture.

sources.title: Alice Springs Town Council, A Brief History
sources.note: Local-government history checked for Mparntwe, Arrernte custodianship, present language teaching, the 1861 to 62 Stuart expedition, and telegraph naming.

sources.title: AIATSIS, AustLang overview
sources.note: National Indigenous institute resource checked for language and variety identifiers, naming, and precise catalogue use.

sources.title: AIATSIS, AustLang help
sources.note: AIATSIS guidance checked for complex and contested language, dialect, spelling, and group relationships.

sources.title: Arrernte Angkentye Online, About the Eastern and Central Arrernte Learners’ List
sources.note: Community-language source checked for Arrernte reference-group guidance, speaker involvement, senior compiler Veronica Perrurle Dobson, and community copyright.

sources.title: Arrernte Angkentye Online, Eastern and Central Arrernte Learners’ List
sources.note: Community-language learner resource checked for public modern terms concerning water, foods, windbreaks, tools, and learning.

sources.title: IAD Press, Anpernirrentye: Kin and Skin
sources.note: Arrernte Elder and co-authored public guide checked for relationships among family, language, land, ancestral responsibility, and respect.

sources.title: IAD Press, Arrernte Traditional Healing
sources.note: Arrernte-authored public source checked for Land, spirit, Angangkere healers, singing, touch, and plant knowledge without clinical extrapolation.

sources.title: Ecology and Society, Anpernirrentye framework
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Arrernte-collaborative study checked for relations among people, land, resource species, and spiritual domains.

sources.title: Akeyulerre, Programs
sources.note: Arrernte-led source checked for Elders directing healing, language, family-on-Country work, and intergenerational responsibilities today.

sources.title: Children’s Ground, Evaluation of Ampe-kenhe Ahelhe 2017 to 2019
sources.note: Arrernte-led evaluation checked for Elders, First Language, on-Country learning, listening, watching, talking, family health, and access to healers.

sources.title: Children’s Ground, Central Australia
sources.note: Community source checked for Central, Eastern, and Western Arrernte-led learning with children, families, First Language, and Country.

sources.title: Learning Communities, Arrernte research realities
sources.note: Arrernte scholar’s critique checked for frontier research, displaced authority, extracted ritual knowledge, and public-versus-restricted evidence.

sources.title: NT Government, Finke Gorge National Park Joint Management Plan
sources.note: Joint-management plan checked for plural Arrernte identities, pmere responsibilities, reliable water, long occupation, travel, food, mission chronology, and dispossession.

sources.title: NT Government, Napwerte / Ewaninga Rock Carvings Conservation Reserve
sources.note: Official source checked for ancient Arrernte engravings, restricted men’s knowledge, unknown public age and meaning, and respectful access rules.

sources.title: Cambridge University Press, The Archaeology of Deserts: Australia in Context
sources.note: Academic synthesis checked for water-limited mobility, Arandic distinctiveness, desert diversity, durable traces, and regional-model limits.

sources.title: Cambridge University Press, A chain of connection
sources.note: Academic chapter checked for interior exchange networks and the need for local evidence before naming specific Arrernte routes or goods.

sources.title: ANU Press, The Aranda’s Pepa, chapter 1
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis checked for Western Arandic varieties, non-hard boundaries, early 1870s recorded encounters, and pastoral pressure.

sources.title: History Trust of South Australia, The Overland Telegraph Line
sources.note: Institutional history checked against archival diaries for 1870 to 75 trespass, resistance, diplomacy, flood damage, water, stations, camps, and vocabulary records.

sources.title: National Museum of Australia, Overland Telegraph
sources.note: National museum chronology checked for Stuart’s route, 1870 to 72 construction, station networks, and earlier Aboriginal pathways.

sources.title: NT Government, Alice Springs Telegraph Station Historical Reserve
sources.note: Official site chronology checked for the 1872 station, permanent water, and the first sustained European settlement at Alice Springs.

sources.title: Australian Government, Hermannsburg Historic Precinct
sources.note: National heritage source checked for the 1877 mission on Western Arrernte Country, later assimilation structures, refuge, conflict, and artistic continuity.

sources.title: Australian Historical Studies, Early German-Aboriginal Encounters at Hermannsburg, 1877 to 91
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study checked for cautious early encounters, mission discipline, the 1879 ration start, and chiefly post-1880 intensification of local pastoral violence.

sources.title: AIATSIS, Mission and reserve records
sources.note: AIATSIS archive guide checked for Hermannsburg dates and warnings about missionary and commemorative institutional bias.

sources.title: AIATSIS, Arrernte Returns
sources.note: Community-led government source checked for returned restricted objects, senior custodianship, songs, future generations, and 2019 and 2021 ceremonies.

sources.title: Central Land Council, Land won back
sources.note: Aboriginal land-council chronology checked for Eastern Arrernte land return, long dispossession, and living cultural authority.

sources.title: MCSCA and Alice Springs Town Council, A Welcome to Mparntwe
sources.note: Official booklet checked for a modern Central Arrernte acknowledgement, paired English rendering, Mparntwe place names, and Alice Springs Language Centre translation credit.

sources.title: National Museum of Australia, Artefacts from Central Australia
sources.note: National museum object histories checked for later Arrernte-attributed material, a child’s bark toy shield, collection dates, and collector bias.

sources.title: NT Government, Lhere Mparntwe Management Strategy 2019
sources.note: Contemporary collaborative strategy checked for the Todd and Charles river systems, Traditional Owner authority, fire, rubbish, erosion, and Country care.

sources.title: E. M. Curr, The Australian Race, volumes 1–2 (1886; Library and Archives NT scan)
sources.note: Government-library scan checked for the nineteenth-century Arrernte vocabulary published in Curr’s comparative compilation and the colonial form of that record.

sources.title: History SA, Telegraph
sources.note: South Australian public-history source checked for the 1870 to 1872 overland telegraph project, continental connection, and colonial infrastructure.

sources.title: State Library of South Australia, Kookaburra sits on the telegraph wire
sources.note: State-library history checked for Stuart’s route, the 1870 to 1872 construction phase, Aboriginal trade routes, unceded Country, and disruption.
